sections.h2: Where is the Ingham County Register of Deeds, and why is it in Mason?
sections.html:
The Ingham County Register of Deeds is at 341 S. Jefferson Street, 2nd Floor, Mason, MI 48854, with a mailing address of PO Box 195, Mason, MI 48854. The phone is 517-676-7216. Mason is the county seat even though Lansing, the state capital, lies largely inside Ingham County. Lansing is the only state capital in the country that does not also serve as its county seat.

The office contact page lists counter hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The vault, where older records are kept, opens 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays by appointment, so call before driving out from Lansing or East Lansing.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Ingham County?
sections.html:
The county's fee schedule charges $30.00 to record a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified copy of a court document or other real property instrument, regardless of the number of pages. The other charges are small but they add up if several papers are filed on one closing day.

  • $3.00 for each liber and page or instrument number listed on a document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument.
  • $0.50 a page for a time-stamped copy, offered only when the document is presented for recording.
  • $1.00 a page for copies of recorded documents.
  • $5.00 per document plus $1.00 a page for a certified copy of a recorded document.

Fees are due when the document is recorded, as MCL 600.2567 provides.

sections.h2: Do I need a tax certificate before recording an Ingham County deed?
sections.html:
Yes, for the deeds that carry a warranty. The register's fee page says a tax certificate from the County Treasurer's Office must be in hand before the office will record a warranty deed, covenant deed, land contract or land contract assignment with a warranty clause. The same rule applies to an affidavit correcting the legal description of one of those papers, and to condominium master deeds, including amendments that change the legal description.

The certificate costs $5.00 for the first five parcel numbers and $0.20 for each additional parcel, citing MCL 211.135. A seller with a split parcel or several tax IDs should count them ahead of time. The Treasurer can be reached at 517-676-7220.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax handled on an Ingham County sale?
sections.html:
Ingham County's fee page puts the state tax at $3.75 per $500 and the county tax at $0.55 per $500. It says the tax falls on the seller or grantor and is paid when the instrument is presented for recording. A deed has to state the total consideration on its face, or a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit goes in with it. Any exemption must be written on the instrument.

The register's page adds three details that come up in practice:

  • A sale of land in more than one county must split the price by parcel, and each county collects on its share.
  • A foreclosure instrument owes county transfer tax on the sale price it states.
  • A conveyance of an easement or right of way is taxable.

The exemption lists are in MCL 207.505 and MCL 207.526.

sections.h2: What does the Ingham County office check on a deed?
sections.html:
The recording requirements page stresses that the list is not complete, but it covers the common stumbling blocks:

  • Original signatures, with names typed or printed under them in black or dark blue ink.
  • A notary block showing the notary's signature, county and state of commission, commission expiration date, and the place where the paper was signed.
  • A certified copy of the death certificate, recorded as its own document and cross-referenced, whenever "survivor" is indicated.
  • Court orders that are certified with the clerk's raised seal.
  • No white-out or correction tape anywhere on the document.
  • A 2.5 inch top margin on page one and no more than the last four digits of a Social Security number.

These track MCL 565.201 and related sections, and the state text is at legislature.mi.gov.

sections.h2: How do I search Ingham County records?
sections.html: Online index records run from 1956 to the present, with images beginning in 1960. Three tools are offered: a free index search called Direct Search that omits the most recent seven days, Tapestry at $8.95 per search with images printed at $1.00 a page, and Laredo, a subscription for people who do title work regularly. Index data for 1956 to 1981 is still being reviewed for conversion errors, and records in that range are available in the vault by appointment. Copies of documents from before 1960 are available at the office in Mason, at $1.00 per page, in person or by mail to Register of Deeds Copies, P.O. Box 195, Mason, MI 48854.

sections.h2: Which other Ingham County offices touch a home sale?
sections.html:
The county's home page lists direct numbers for the offices a seller is most likely to need. Use them to line up paperwork before the closing date rather than on the day.

  • Treasurer, 517-676-7220: tax certificates and the tax status of a parcel.
  • Register of Deeds, 517-676-7216: recording, copies and vault appointments.
  • Probate Court, 517-483-6300: estate matters when the owner has died and the house passes through probate.
  • 30th Judicial Circuit Court, 517-483-6500: court orders and judgments that may need to be recorded against a property.

The courthouse address shown on the county site is 341 S. Jefferson, Mason, MI 48854. An Equalization department also appears in the county's department list for questions about valuation.

sections.h2: What should an Ingham County seller know about the area?
sections.html:
Ingham County was created by the Michigan Territorial Legislature on October 29, 1829, attached to Washtenaw County, and given its own government in 1838. It covers 556 square miles of land, and it is named for Samuel D. Ingham, Treasury secretary under Andrew Jackson. The Grand River runs along the western edge and the Red Cedar River crosses the north. Michigan State University, Lansing Community College and the Lansing Lugnuts are here.

Cities are East Lansing and Lansing (both partly), Leslie, Mason and Williamston. Dansville, Stockbridge and Webberville are villages, and Haslett, Holt and Okemos are census-designated places. Census Bureau figures put the 2025 population at 289,709 and the housing stock at 127,510 units. Owners hold 59.5 percent of homes, the median value is $198,800, median rent is $1,084 and median household income is $65,526. The share of adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree is 41.2 percent.

faqs.q: What are the Ingham County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Counter hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The vault is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. by appointment, so phone 517-676-7216 to schedule a visit.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on an Ingham County home sale?
faqs.a: The seller or grantor pays, according to the county fee schedule. The tax is due when the deed is presented for recording, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county.

faqs.q: Do I need anything from the Treasurer before my deed can be recorded?
faqs.a: Yes, a tax certificate is required before the register will record a warranty deed, covenant deed or land contract. It costs $5.00 for up to five parcel numbers and $0.20 for each one beyond that.

faqs.q: Can I search Ingham County deeds for free?
faqs.a: Yes. Direct Search is a free index search covering 1956 to the present except for the last seven days. Viewing the document images through Tapestry costs $8.95 a search, plus $1.00 a page to print.

faqs.q: Is the Ingham County courthouse in Lansing?
faqs.a: No, the Register of Deeds is in Mason at 341 S. Jefferson Street, 2nd Floor. Lansing sits mostly inside the county, but Mason is the county seat.
